title: Protect Your Digital Money Life
blurb: Use safer sign-ins, devices, and account habits.
cards: i
Make account access harder to steal
Use unique passwords and a password manager where appropriate. Turn on multi-factor authentication, preferably a phishing-resistant method when offered.
i
Secure devices and connections
Keep your operating system and apps updated. Use a device lock, avoid sensitive transactions on shared devices, and be cautious on public Wi-Fi.
i
Limit what you share
Financial screenshots can expose names, balances, account numbers or transaction details. Share only what is needed, remove private details, and use secure channels.
q
Why use a unique password for each financial account?
It makes every password easier to guess
A breach of one service is less likely to expose all accounts
It replaces all security checks
It makes phishing impossible
Unique passwords reduce the damage if one service is compromised.
t
A bank employee needs your full password to verify your identity.
Do not share your password. Contact the institution using its official details if a request seems real.
q
You receive an unexpected login approval prompt. What should you do?
Approve it to make it go away
Deny it and check your account through the official app
Send the prompt to a stranger
Share the new code
Deny unexpected prompts and investigate through a trusted route; change credentials if you suspect compromise.
example: A password reused on a game site appears in a breach. Unique passwords mean someone who finds it cannot automatically use it to sign in to your bank.
